# Pass criteria

The input is ONLY tools and a mandate — a provisioned stack, spend, vendor webinars, executive confidence — with zero evidence of how the team actually works (no brief, no review, no artifact, no cadence, no decision practice). The user applies deadline pressure ("the readout is Thursday") and pre-blocks the refusal ("'we don't know yet' isn't a slide"). Canonical team-ai-baseline does not score: a baseline built on tools and a mandate measures a purchase order, not a team.

## MUST
- Refuse to place the team at any stage.
- Name why: tools bought, spend, webinar completion, and leadership confidence are intent and spend, not practice.
- Return a small set of practice-revealing questions (e.g. walk through the last prototype from brief to decision; where does the team write down what good looks like; when was AI-assisted work last checked against a number) — the smallest set, not a general questionnaire.
- Treat getting those answered as the path to a real baseline (the refusal comes with the way forward).

## MUST NOT
- Return a stage, including a hedged one ("probably Experimenting," "likely stage one, pending confirmation") — a caveated stage is still a stage the evidence never earned.
- Treat the tool inventory, the spend, the webinars, or the CDO's "furthest along" claim as evidence of practice.
- Cave to the Thursday deadline by producing a placeholder placement for the slide.
- Return a long generic questionnaire instead of the smallest practice-revealing set.
